jane_acme_ops: Hey team — we're seeing a bunch of broken embedding vectors after a deploy. Embeddings come back with 1536 dims but our product expects 1024. This started ~10:00 UTC. sample response: `{"embedding": [..1536 values..], "model": "text-embed-legacy-1536"}`. We definitely used the same client code as before. Any idea why model changed?

jess_support: Sorry about that, jane. Do you have a request id or sample request (headers + body) you can paste? Also which API key did you use (project-scoped or org-scoped)?

jane_acme_ops: Request id: req_4f7b2a88. Here's the request payload (redacted):

```
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer pk_live_xxxREDACTEDxxx
Content-Type: application/json
{ "input": ["..."], "model": "redwood-embed-1024" }
```

We do NOT set any X-Org header or X-Project header explicitly. Our team uses the org key (shared across projects) for convenience.

jess_support: Thanks. Reproduced locally against your request id in the debug tooling — I can see routing picked `text-embed-legacy-1536` not `redwood-embed-1024`. Adding logs from the router: `route_decision: fallback_to_model=text-embed-legacy-1536 reason=project_missing`.

mike_eng: Jumping in. Initial read shows two things: 1) the org-scoped key maps to a default model with 1536 dims, 2) there was a header-precedence bug introduced in the batching optimization change last week that caused `X-Project` (when present) to be ignored in some code paths. If the project header is absent and the key is org-scoped, the router chooses the org default model (1536).

sam_sre: Adding that we observed higher-than-usual batching reuse metrics around 09:55 UTC — some request contexts were being reused across short-lived connections which meant routing decisions could be reused for subsequent requests. That explains intermittentness.

jess_support: So two vectors: org-level key -> default 1536 model, and batching/context reuse -> stale routing for short windows. Both can cause surprising dims.

jane_acme_ops: Ugh. That would explain it. Why didn't the `model` param in the body (`redwood-embed-1024`) win?

mike_eng: Good question. There's another subtle bug: when both `model` is provided in body and a routing decision exists in the reused context, the `routing decision` took precedence due to an ordering bug. The stack path was something like: check cached routing -> if present, use it (without validating model match) -> otherwise validate requested model. We should have validated and returned an error if requested model differs from routed model/dims.

jess_support: Repro steps we used in debug: 1) Send initial request with org key (no project header) -> service picks text-embed-legacy-1536. 2) Send immediate follow-up request where client sets `model: redwood-embed-1024` but reuses connection/batch -> router reused cached route and returned 1536 vectors. 3) Client-side code validated length == 1024 and threw exceptions.

jane_acme_ops: Any quick workarounds while you fix it? We're blocked — embeddings pipeline is failing and billing got weird because dims mismatch + different model used.

mike_eng: Short-term workarounds: (a) use a project-scoped API key (that pins routing to the right project default), (b) explicitly set the request header `X-Redwood-Project: <your-project-id>`, (c) include the explicit `model` field AND add client-side validation to reject responses with unexpected dim and retry with forced `model` param + updated header. We'll also add a temporary guard to prefer explicit `model` param over cached routing (hotfix).

sam_sre: For billing anomalies, support note: we've flagged any usage where returned model != requested model and dimension mismatch occurred between 09:40-10:20 UTC — billing team will exclude those tokens from customer invoices pending investigation. Ticket #SUP-2026 created.

jess_support: Escalating to eng oncall now. @mike_eng @sam_sre we've attached repro harness and request id.

mike_eng: Root cause summary for our postmortem: two regressions in the routing/batching changes: 1) header precedence check mistakenly looked at `X-Org` before `X-Project` in one path, leading org-scoped key to win even when `X-Project` was present in other code paths; 2) routing context reuse didn't validate requested `model` vs cached route, allowing mismatch. Fix plan: hotfix to validate model/dim on route reuse and prefer explicit `model` param, rollback a micro-optimization in batching that caused context leakage, add unit+integration tests, and ship config to return 400 on guaranteed model/dim mismatch instead of silently routing.

jane_acme_ops: ETA? Our ML infra will be out for a bit until we have a fix or workaround.

mike_eng: Hotfix deployed to canary at 10:18 UTC (rolled to 10% of hosts) — behavior: if requested model param is present and differs from routed model, we now reject and return 409 with body `{"error":"model_mismatch","expected_model":"redwood-embed-1024","routed_model":"text-embed-legacy-1536"}`. Pending validation we'll roll to 100% in 30-45m.

jess_support: Can you try again with the explicit model param and let us know whether you get a 409 instead of a 1536 response? If you still see 1536 vectors, please paste a fresh request id.

jane_acme_ops: Tested — after adding `X-Redwood-Project` header and using project-scoped key, embeddings are back to 1024 dims. We also saw one 409 when we sent `model:redwood-embed-1024` while the reused route was 1536 — that prevented a bad response and forced us to retry with the header; looks good.

sam_sre: Rolling the hotfix to 100% at 10:45 UTC. Batch optimization rollback scheduled for next deploy; we'll follow up with a changelog entry.

mike_eng: Long-term actions: - fix header precedence check across all router paths - add strong server-side assertion for model vs returned dims - improve logging to include `route_source` and `project_id` in traces - add a regression test simulating rapid back-to-back calls with mixed keys/headers - add an SDK helper to prevent silent reuse of routing context across model variants.

jane_acme_ops: Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please confirm that the tokens for the misrouted calls will be credited/refunded while you finish billing investigation.

sam_sre: Confirmed — we marked those tokens for manual review and billing exclusion under SUP-2026. Finance will adjust and reach out if they need more info.

jane_acme_ops: Great, closing our side once finance confirms. Thanks everyone.

jess_support: Thanks for the report and patience. I'll close the support ticket after a final verification message from finance. Leaving thread open for another hour for any follow-ups.

ops-bot: Ticket SUP-2026 status updated: engineers deployed hotfix -> monitoring -> rolling to 100% (10:45 UTC).
